=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml: lines 489-498 (the `managed_integration_merge` block) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `[[ "${PR_BASE_REF}" == orchestrator/project-* ]]` glob match is the first clause of an OR, so it short-circuits to true for ANY `orchestrator/project-*` branch regardless of whether it matches the managed child's declared integration branch.
  WHY: A managed issue whose body declares `Integration branch: orchestrator/project-9` can be labeled `ai:merged`, closed, and have its lineage finalised by a PR that merged into `orchestrator/project-10`; the cited test only exercises a `claude/*` base ref and does not cover a different `orchestrator/project-*` base ref.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh: line 2075 (the `[^[:alnum:]_#?]` boundary class inside `extract_repo_scoped_issue_refs_from_text`) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The new boundary character class excludes both `#` and `?` after the issue number, rejecting query-only issue URLs as well as fragment URLs.
  WHY: A PR body or title referencing an issue only via a query-bearing URL will be silently dropped, leaving the referenced issue's labels, state, and lineage untouched; the cited test covers a combined query-and-fragment case but not a query-only URL.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Tests. Cover the following in the existing `issue_pr_status` test module, or a new one registered in `ci.yml`: a PR merged into a non-default branch with only `Refs #N` plus a comment URL leaves #N's labels unchanged and does not finalize its lineage; an orchestrator-managed child merged into its integration branch still gets `ai:merged` and is closed; a default-branch merge with `Fixes #N` still labels and closes; a comment URL alone yields no linked issue."
  Expected change site: `tests/test_issue_pr_status_payload_fallback_contract.py` (test registration in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`) and the test job environments that execute the test module.
  Evidence of absence: The PR adds the four required behavioural tests (plus extras), all gated by `_jq_missing(...)` which calls `pytest.skip(message)` when `shutil.which("jq") is None`. The two CI test jobs that run this module (`tests-heal-plan-and-validation` and `tests-promote-stall-and-review`) install only `yamllint coverage pyyaml jsonschema jinja2 pytest ruff` — `jq` is not listed and not pre-installed on the runner images, so the suite reports `11 passed, 8 skipped` and `jq`-dependent assertions are never executed in CI. The required test coverage is therefore added on paper but not exercised by the gate that decides whether the PR merges, defeating the purpose of the tests the issue spec demands.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
